scoring_notice: All scores are analyst judgments, not survey-derived probabilities, investment advice, or proof of willingness to pay. Evidence eligibility checks presence, not truth, independence, geography, freshness, or commercial validation.

undated_sources.finding: Official SDK documentation provides native approval primitives; this is engineering context and a commoditization warning. No publication date asserted.
Accounting workflow plans at $74–$149/user/month are an adjacent category benchmark, not willingness to buy this add-on. No publication date asserted.

opportunities.title: Human-reviewed AI client briefs for small professional-services firms
opportunities.buyer: Operations lead or managing partner at a 5–50-person bookkeeping or advisory firm
opportunities.problem: AI-assisted client drafts lack a lightweight review record tied to the exact approved version.

evidence.finding: July 2026 survey of 5,067 U.S. adults: AI users ranked accuracy 45%, trustworthiness 40%, and security/privacy 36% among choice factors. Consumer signal, not evidence of a bookkeeping firm's software budget.
2025 report says 58% of surveyed small businesses use generative AI, versus 40% in 2024. Adoption is not demand for this product.

Retained engineering-risk evidence from the prior decision: GAO describes inaccurate outputs and privacy/security risks. Government-focused risk corroboration, not SME purchasing evidence. Today's current SDK/competitor observations are recorded separately as undated sources.

opportunities.commercial_hypothesis: Offer a paid 30-day pilot for one client-brief workflow. Interview 10–15 firms; proceed only if at least two agree to paid pilots and can demonstrate recurring review pain.
opportunities.kill_criterion: Stop or change niche if interviews find no recurring problem, no budget owner, or existing bundled tools solve the workflow adequately.
opportunities.competition_risk: Platform governance suites and provider-native controls may bundle the feature. SDK-native approval primitives make a simple approval log copyable; a review log alone is not a moat.
opportunities.geography_limit: Initial evidence is U.S. consumer/SMB, not validation of Indian demand.

opportunities.title: Invoice reconciliation and approved follow-up queue
opportunities.buyer: Owner/bookkeeper at a small B2B agency or consultancy
opportunities.problem: Overdue invoices and mismatched partial payments require manual review before sending accurate reminders.

evidence.finding: Intuit's January 2025 survey of 2,487 U.S. businesses with 0–100 employees: 56% were owed unpaid invoices, averaging $17,500; 47% had some invoices overdue over 30 days. Survey association, not causal impact or willingness to buy.

The unpaid-invoice problem motivates an engineering hypothesis: robust partial-payment, credit and dispute matching must precede reminder generation. The source does not benchmark reconciliation difficulty.

opportunities.competition_risk: Accounting vendors and AR tools already own integrations and provide reminders; generic reminder generation is poorly differentiated. Clearer pain does not establish product-specific willingness to pay or defensibility.
opportunities.commercial_hypothesis: Validate cross-system exceptions with five bookkeepers before building an accounting integration.
opportunities.geography_limit: Evidence is U.S.-focused and does not establish Indian demand.

opportunities.title: Unused subscription detection and cancellation follow-through
opportunities.buyer: U.S. consumer managing recurring household subscriptions
opportunities.problem: Consumers may continue paying for subscriptions they rarely use and need to identify and stop unwanted recurring charges.

evidence.finding: CNET/YouGov June 2025 survey of 2,440 respondents estimated $204/year in unused subscriptions. This indicates reported consumer waste, not willingness to pay a separate detector.

Turning reported unused subscriptions into reliable savings would require identifying recurring charges and supporting effective cancellation; the survey does not assess data-access feasibility, detection accuracy, or cancellation outcomes.

The survey's unused-subscription estimate does not demonstrate a gap versus bank/card account features or existing subscription-management services; willingness to pay, distribution and differentiation remain weakly evidenced.

opportunities.competition_risk: Potential substitutes include bank/card transaction features and existing subscription-management services; transaction access and cancellation follow-through create trust and execution burdens.
opportunities.commercial_hypothesis: Do not build before testing whether consumers will pay for verified net savings and whether access/cancellation can be delivered reliably.
opportunities.geography_limit: Evidence is U.S. consumer survey data, not validation in India or another market.
